name: AAVATAR Therapeutics
summary: Machine learning-driven AAV capsid engineering platform with in-house CMC manufacturing for tissue-specific gene therapy delivery.
content:
Company Overview # AAVATAR Therapeutics is an AI-driven AAV capsid engineering company developing next-generation gene delivery platforms for rare and intractable diseases. The company combines a machine learning-based capsid engineering platform with in-house AAV manufacturing capabilities to enable rapid design, production, and validation of tissue-targeted AAV vectors. AAVATAR is positioned as a platform company focused on capsid licensing and co-development with pharmaceutical partners.
Technology & Product # AAVATAR’s core technology is a machine learning-driven AAV capsid engineering platform that prioritizes manufacturability while identifying high-performing tissue-targeted capsids. Large-scale capsid libraries are screened using next-generation sequencing and iteratively optimized through rodent and non-human primate validation. The platform is integrated with in-house AAV manufacturing capabilities covering vector design, process optimization, quality control, and scalable nonclinical production, enabling rapid discovery and validation of licensing-ready AAV capsid assets.
Market & Use Cases # AAVATAR develops AI-engineered AAV capsid platforms for tissue-specific in vivo gene delivery. The current strategic focus is on CNS, heart, skeletal muscle, and kidney targeting. Proof-of-platform programs include Krabbe disease, hereditary hearing loss, and geographic atrophy (GA). Beyond these indications, the platform can be rapidly adapted to additional tissues such as the PNS and pancreas according to partner needs. The company’s business model is centered on capsid platform licensing and co-development with pharmaceutical partners.
Traction & References # AAVATAR raised a KRW 5 billion Series A in late 2023, led by TS Investment with Shinhan Capital, Smilegate Investment, and Wonik Investment Partners joining(BioSpectator). It was selected as a government Baby Unicorn company in 2024(AAVATAR). AAVATAR runs research collaborations with academic and medical partners including Ewha Womans University, Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and Samsung Medical Center(AAVATAR).
Collaboration Relevance # AAVATAR is well positioned for collaborations with pharmaceutical companies and academic institutions through joint validation, MTAs, sponsored research, co-development, and platform licensing. The company is currently advancing CNS, heart, skeletal muscle, and kidney targeting programs while maintaining a flexible platform that can be adapted to additional tissues and therapeutic indications based on partner needs.

name: ABR
summary: Sustainable lithium-ion battery direct recycling technology using water and ultrasonic waves.
content:
Company Overview # ABR recycles lithium-ion battery manufacturing scrap and end-of-life batteries. Its direct recycling method uses water and ultrasonic waves to recover battery-grade materials. The process avoids high-temperature smelting and harsh chemicals.
Technology & Product # ABR offers direct recycling services and remanufactured battery materials:
Direct Recycling Process: ABR uses water and ultrasonic waves to separate active cathode and anode materials from foil substrates in battery manufacturing scrap. Remanufactured Cathode Materials: High-purity recycled cathode powders (such as NCM) reclaimed directly from manufacturing waste. Remanufactured Anode Material: A recycled anode powder produced by recovering anode active materials from battery manufacturing process scrap and regenerating them for reuse in battery production. Recycled Activated Carbon: Carbon-based materials extracted and prepared for industrial adsorption and energy applications. Market & Use Cases # ABR serves battery manufacturing gigafactories and battery recycling companies. These customers need to manage production scrap and build closed-loop material supply chains. Because ABR recovers active materials directly, its process uses less energy and produces less carbon than hydrometallurgical or pyrometallurgical recycling.
Traction & References # Ongoing Direct Recycling PoC with global battery manufacturers → Technical validation and business collaboration with PowerCo SE (Volkswagen Group, Germany) and Exide Energy Solutions (India) Awarded “Green Battery Innovation Leader – South Korea 2025” Established a global-standard quality management system based on ISO 9001, ensuring reliable production and supply capabilities Collaboration Relevance # Battery cell makers can collaborate with ABR to process and reuse cathode and anode scrap directly within their production facilities. EV manufacturers and electronics companies can run joint PoCs to assess the electrochemical performance of ABR’s remanufactured active materials in test cells. Material suppliers looking to establish low-carbon supply chains can integrate ABR’s direct recycling technology into their recovery pipelines.

name: Ainex Corporation
summary: Real-time AI software for upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy that detects lesions and provides diagnostic support during procedures.
content:
Company Overview # Ainex Corporation is a medical AI software company specializing in gastrointestinal endoscopy. The company is dedicated to developing AI technology that enhances clinicians’ diagnostic accuracy and ultimately saves patients’ lives. Its flagship product, ENAD, integrates seamlessly into the endoscopy workflow to detect abnormal lesions in real time and provide actionable diagnostic insights.
Technology & Product # The core product is ENAD, an AI-assisted diagnostic software for both upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy. The system operates on existing endoscopy monitors without requiring specialized hardware, linking via a simple connection module. For lower GI procedures, ENAD CADe detects colon polyps in real time, while ENAD CADx categorizes the detected polyps into adenoma/neoplasm, hyperplastic polyp, or sessile serrated lesion.
Market & Use Cases # Ainex targets gastroenterologists and internal medicine departments conducting routine endoscopic screenings. By deploying ENAD, hospitals can improve the detection rates of hard-to-spot polyps and adenomas, reducing the risk of missed diagnoses during high-volume endoscopy sessions.
Traction & References # ENAD has been adopted by more than 130 hospitals in Korea and over 30 global institutions. The software demonstrates robust clinical performance, improving the adenoma detection rate by 16.2%p with ENAD CADe. ENAD CADx classifies detected polyps — adenoma/neoplasm, hyperplastic polyp, or sessile serrated lesion — with over 90% accuracy. ENAD CADx has obtained Class III medical device approval from the MFDS in Korea and passed the Innovative Medical Device integrated review in 2025, and was designated an innovative product by Korea’s Public Procurement Service (PPS) in April 2026. The product has also been approved and commercialized in seven countries, including Thailand, Singapore, and Vietnam. In January 2026, Ainex signed an MOU with Olympus Korea to expand ENAD’s domestic business(Ainex Press).
Collaboration Relevance # Ainex is well-positioned for distribution and integration partnerships with global endoscopy equipment manufacturers (such as Olympus, Pentax, or Fujifilm). The company is also a strong candidate for collaborative research with global medical institutions seeking to implement and validate AI-assisted endoscopy diagnostics in diverse patient populations.

name: AIT Studio
summary: An iPad-based medical device that uses AI to analyze how a person walks from a single camera, with no body sensors.
content:
Company Overview # AIT Studio is a digital healthcare company that turns a single camera into a clinical-grade tool for gait analysis. The founding team comes from KAIST mechanical engineering. Its members have backgrounds in automotive computer vision, consulting, and biomechanics. The company holds one of Korea’s largest collections of walking data. It builds its products around movement checks that are fast and easy to access.
Technology & Product # The main product is MEDISTEP, a walking-analysis device that runs on an iPad. It is markerless, which means nothing is attached to the body: no wearables and no external sensors. The AI runs right on the device and reads how the joints across the whole body move, using just one camera. In about one minute, it produces about 40 walking metrics, such as walking speed, stride length, balance, and joint angles. The product line consists of MEDISTEP M Pro, a Class I medical device for hospitals and clinics, and MEDISTEP M, a non-medical version for fitness, senior care, and wellness settings. It delivers approximately 95% accuracy compared to gold-standard motion-capture systems (Vicon, Qualisys, GAITRite), verified through third-party testing, at a small fraction of their cost.
Market & Use Cases # MEDISTEP is used by hospitals, rehabilitation clinics, elderly and senior care, and public health screening. The technology works well for quick mobility checks in places where traditional motion labs are too slow or too expensive. That makes it a good fit for both clinical assessments and large-scale community health screening.
Traction & References # AIT Studio is expanding into the North American and European markets with MEDISTEP(BioTimes). In Korea, MEDISTEP M and M Pro have completed domestic medical device filing (Class I notification)(Newswire). MEDISTEP holds CE-MDR Class I certification and ISO 13485 certification, with an EU Authorized Representative in place in Germany. The company raised a Pre-Series A funding round led by Bluepoint Partners, with East Gate Partners and MAGNA Investment also taking part(WOWTALE). MEDISTEP is now used by several major Korean university hospitals, including Asan Medical Center, and by Felix Platter Hospital, a university geriatric and rehabilitation hospital in Basel, Switzerland. AIT Studio unveiled the MEDISTEP series at CES 2025(Newswire). It also received NET (New Excellent Technology) certification and was designated a 2025 Innovation Product by Korea’s Public Procurement Service, the government agency that buys products for public use(Newswire). It is part of the IBK Changgong Mapo cohort(Tech42).
Collaboration Relevance # AIT Studio is a strong fit for European clinical testing, for use in hospitals and rehabilitation centers, and for distribution partnerships. Its early clinical work in Switzerland makes it easier for European partners to get started. A proven track record in Korean university hospitals, along with its public technology credentials, makes it a credible partner for clinics and distributors moving into new markets.

name: APGREEN
summary: Distributed on-site hydrogen and power solutions that leverage existing gas infrastructure, based on CPOX reforming and fuel-cell integration.
content:
Company Overview # APGREEN is a distributed on-site hydrogen and power solution company that leverages existing gas infrastructure. The company combines Catalytic Partial Oxidation (CPOX) reforming and fuel cells to produce hydrogen and electricity directly at customer facilities from city gas, LNG, or biomethane — without the need for large-scale hydrogen delivery infrastructure.
Technology & Product # APGREEN manufactures the APG-Series, a containerized hydrogen production and power system:
CPOX Reforming (Catalytic Partial Oxidation): The system reforms city gas, LNG, or biomethane into hydrogen with low energy use and high thermal efficiency. Fuel-Cell Integration: Hydrogen feeds directly into integrated fuel cells to generate electricity on-site. Modular Design: The APG-Series uses an all-in-one container design (models APG-5, APG-20, APG-100, and APG-300) that is mobile and easy to install. Hydrogen produced from city gas or LNG is natural-gas-based. When biomethane is used as the feedstock, the same systems enable a low-carbon hydrogen pathway.
Market & Use Cases # APGREEN targets distributed energy consumers, hydrogen refueling stations, industrial plants, fuel-cell power generators, and biogas processing facilities. The modular containers let operators generate electricity and hydrogen locally, cutting transportation and logistics costs.
Traction & References # APGREEN holds 20 patents in total — 9 applied and 11 pending(APGREEN). APGREEN won the H2 Innovation Award (Hydrogen Production category) and the Best Product Media Award Excellent Pick at the World Hydrogen Expo (WHE) 2025(Venture Square). Collaboration Relevance # Refueling station operators and industrial facilities can run PoCs with modular APG units to test on-site hydrogen sourcing and reduce delivery reliance. Agricultural and waste management operations can partner with APGREEN to convert waste biogas into electricity or high-purity hydrogen. European and global utilities that need local grid support or backup generators can deploy the APG-Series as a distributed power node. For European research institutes, APGREEN is open to joint CPOX R&D, reformer optimization, fuel-cell-grade hydrogen validation, and pilot demonstration projects.

name: BANF
summary: Intelligent tire system company combining tire-mounted sensors, wireless power, and fleet data analytics.
content:
Company Overview # BANF builds intelligent tire and road data systems for commercial vehicles, fleets, EVs, and autonomous driving. Its system turns tires into real-time sensors for tire condition, vehicle safety, and road surface data.
The product goes beyond standard tire pressure monitoring. BANF combines tire sensors, wireless power, and analytics software. Fleets, OEMs, tire companies, and road operators can use the data for safety, uptime, maintenance, fuel efficiency, and road insight.
Technology & Product # BANF’s Tire Profile System has three main parts:
iSensor: a tire-mounted sensor with 3-axis acceleration sensing, TPMS, and low-power Bluetooth. Smart Profiler: a data hub and wireless power source for sensors inside fast-rotating tires. Data Viewer: an interface for reviewing tire and road data. The platform measures tire pressure, temperature, tread condition, wheel alignment, tire load, road surface condition, and lug nut loosening. It offers faster updates and a wider data set than standard TPMS.
Market & Use Cases # BANF is relevant to OEMs, fleet operators, logistics companies, tire companies, intelligent transport systems, and road operators. For these customers, tire condition affects safety, cost, uptime, energy use, and road management.
Key use cases include tire tread monitoring, overload detection, wheel alignment checks, lug nut alerts, road surface data, and predictive maintenance for heavy-duty vehicles. The business model includes SaaS for fleets and trucks. Road operators and OEMs can also use the data analytics layer.
Traction & References # BANF raised a Pre-Series A round totaling KRW 6.5 billion (KRW 4.5 billion in 2022 and a KRW 2 billion follow-on in 2023). Key partners and customers include vehicle makers, tire companies, fleet operators, Nira Dynamics, Hyundai Motor Group, Volvo Group Camp X, DHL, the U.S. Army, and SAE International. Awards and selections include CES 2024 Vehicle Tech & Advanced Mobility Innovation Award, 2023 K-Digital Grand Championship Grand Prize, 2023 IRF Global Road Achievement Awards, TechCrunch Battlefield Top 20, DHL Fastforward Challenge Global Top 3, SAE International GAMIC Top 10, the 2024 Global ICT Future Unicorn program(Money Today), and Forbes Asia 100 To Watch in 2025(Money Today). BANF has pre-production progress and revenue growth through 2025. Collaboration Relevance # Fleet operators, logistics companies, and commercial vehicle platforms can run PoCs around tire safety, uptime, overload prevention, and predictive maintenance. OEMs, tire companies, EV developers, and autonomous vehicle teams can use BANF where vehicle weight, torque, and long operating hours increase tire stress. Road operators and data partners can use tire data for road condition monitoring and infrastructure analytics.

name: BeyondDx
summary: AI blood test for early lung cancer screening that combines multiple serum protein biomarkers with machine learning.
content:
Company Overview # BeyondDx is a precision diagnostics company developing AI-enabled blood-based in vitro diagnostic solutions for cancer and other major disease areas. By integrating multiple circulating biomarkers with artificial intelligence, BeyondDx aims to improve clinical decision-making through earlier, more accurate, and less invasive disease assessment from a single blood sample. Its flagship product, ForeCheck LC, focuses on supporting the management of LDCT-positive pulmonary nodules through biological malignancy risk assessment.
Technology & Product # BeyondDx’s lead product, ForeCheck LC, is a blood-based adjunctive in vitro diagnostic (IVD) designed to assist in assessing the malignancy risk of LDCT-positive pulmonary nodules. Rather than replacing LDCT or providing a definitive diagnosis, the test offers complementary biological risk information to support clinical decisions regarding follow-up imaging, biopsy, or referral.
ForeCheck LC measures three serum protein biomarkers and applies a locked machine-learning algorithm to generate a simple High-Risk or Low-Risk result. The assay is completed in approximately 150 minutes and is integrated into BeyondDx’s iDXGate AI diagnostic platform. Clinical studies have demonstrated encouraging performance in differentiating malignant from benign pulmonary nodules, while earlier studies also showed strong potential for early-stage lung cancer detection.
Market & Use Cases # ForeCheck LC is intended for patients with pulmonary nodules detected by LDCT, where distinguishing benign from malignant nodules remains a major clinical challenge. By providing additional biological risk information, the test aims to support physicians in patient management and potentially reduce unnecessary diagnostic procedures while improving confidence in clinical decision-making.
BeyondDx is currently pursuing Korean regulatory approval while preparing for future CE-IVDR certification by expanding European clinical validation, performance evaluation, and technical documentation. In the longer term, the company’s AI-enabled biomarker platform is expected to expand into companion diagnostics, treatment decision support, recurrence monitoring, and additional disease areas, including mental health disorders.
Traction & References # BeyondDx raised seed funding from Bluepoint Partners and was selected for the DeepTech TIPS program in 2024(The Bio News). The company is also a member of the IBK Changgong(Kpanews), supporting its continued technology and business development.
BeyondDx has established an ISO 13485-certified quality management system and Korean GMP manufacturing capability for in vitro diagnostics(The Yakup). The company has accumulated clinical datasets from more than 3,400 human specimens and has conducted clinical studies and validation work in collaboration with Seoul National University Bundang Hospital. Clinical findings have been presented at ASCO 2025 and ASCO 2026(The Yakup), demonstrating the clinical potential of ForeCheck LC.
In 2025, BeyondDx signed an MOU with Shanghai Kehua Bio-Engineering to pursue joint development and commercialization opportunities for ForeCheck LC, leveraging the partner’s international network across Asia, Europe, and Latin America(The Bio News). The company also received the Grand Prize at the 2025 Women’s Startup Competition organized by Korea’s Ministry of SMEs and Startups(Womennews).
Collaboration Relevance # BeyondDx is seeking long-term collaboration with European hospitals, research institutes, diagnostic laboratories, and industry partners to generate robust clinical evidence in European populations and support future CE-IVDR certification and European market entry. Areas of collaboration include European clinical validation studies, performance evaluation, biobank-based research, joint scientific publications, companion diagnostic development, treatment decision support, and commercialization partnerships.
BeyondDx views Germany as a strategic gateway for building long-term scientific and clinical collaborations. The company believes that high-quality clinical evidence generated together with leading European institutions will be essential for bringing AI-enabled precision diagnostics to patients worldwide.

name: BICHEDAM
summary: A biotech company developing a natural, plant-based pill (BCD101) that the body absorbs well, aimed at treating painful nighttime leg cramps.
content:
Company Overview # BICHEDAM is a biotech company that makes medicines from natural plant ingredients for vascular diseases that come with aging. The company blends traditional Korean medicine with modern drug development standards. It is based in Gyeongsan, Gyeongbuk, and also has branch offices in Seoul and Daegu.
Technology & Product # BICHEDAM’s lead candidate, BCD101, is an oral natural-product-based therapeutic candidate currently developed as a liquid soft-extract formulation. It is based on a standardized six-herb medicinal extract, with puerarin from kudzu root as one of the key marker compounds. BCD101 is designed to modulate vascular and smooth muscle function, with preclinical evidence suggesting involvement of the RhoA/ROCK-related contraction pathway. In simple terms, it aims to help regulate abnormal blood vessel tightening and muscle cramping linked to aging-related vascular dysfunction.
Puerarin has long been known for its vascular and neurovascular pharmacology, but its clinical use as an oral therapy has been limited by poor and variable oral bioavailability. BICHEDAM’s formulation and extraction approach is designed to improve oral systemic exposure of puerarin. In the completed Phase I study, orally administered BCD101 showed measurable systemic exposure of puerarin with a rapid Tmax profile.
Market & Use Cases # BCD101 is aimed at Nocturnal Leg Cramps (NLC), the painful leg cramps that strike at night. Right now, there is no widely accepted drug specifically approved for NLC, so many patients rely on stretching, supplements, or off-label treatments. BICHEDAM sees this gap as a clear unmet need.
The company notes that NLC is common among middle-aged and older adults, especially as vascular aging and circulation problems become more common. BICHEDAM plans to expand its pipeline into other aging-related vascular conditions, including high blood pressure linked to aging and other vascular or neurovascular disorders.
Traction & References # In 2024, BICHEDAM was chosen for TIPS, a Korean government startup support program, which came with KRW 500 million in research funding over two years(Venture Square). The company has raised a total of KRW 2.3 billion across its Seed and Pre-A rounds from multiple institutional investors, including startup investment firms, regional technology holding companies, the Korea Agriculture Policy Insurance & Finance Service, and the Korea Technology Finance Corporation (KIBO). BCD101 received Phase 1 IND approval from Korea’s MFDS, the country’s drug regulator. The trial was run in healthy adults at Chungbuk National University Hospital(BioTimes). BICHEDAM finished this Phase 1 study in 2026, showing good safety and tolerability, and confirmed that puerarin could be measured in the blood after oral dosing with BCD101(K-Job News). The company also licensed know-how from Yeungnam University on how to keep BCD101 high-quality and stable(Yeungnam University). Its patents include a granted US patent (12,329,798 B2), registered Korean patents, and additional applications covering vascular and neurovascular indications(BICHEDAM).
Collaboration Relevance # BICHEDAM is looking for pharmaceutical partners in Europe to discuss how BCD101 could be developed and partnered in the region. The company is especially interested in partners that understand phytomedicine, vascular aging, sleep-related symptoms, and elderly-care markets. BCD101 is a good fit for these discussions because it has completed Phase 1 testing in healthy adults, is taken by mouth as an oral liquid soft-extract formulation, works in a new way, and targets NLC, a condition with no widely accepted drug made specifically for it. The company’s investors, hospital network, and planned Phase II collaboration with Seoul St. Mary’s Hospital show that it is preparing for international clinical and pharmaceutical partnerships.

name: BOOKEND
summary: BOOKEND builds AI proofreading and document-level book-editing software for publishers, editors, and authors, starting in Korea and Japan.
content:
Company Overview # BOOKEND is a Korean publishing-technology company. It builds AI software that automates proofreading and editing work in book publishing. The goal is to cut the time and cost of turning a manuscript into a finished book.
The company runs two products. SENTENCIFY is an AI writing proofreader for editors and authors. “editorial” is a document-level AI book editor for whole manuscripts. BOOKEND also runs its own publishing operation, which gives it a steady revenue base and a real-world testbed for its tools. Its model moves from B2C users (editors, authors, creators) toward B2B customers (publishers and content companies).
BOOKEND is based in Daejeon and works out of Daejeon Startup Park.
Technology & Product # SENTENCIFY is an AI proofreading engine that works sentence by sentence. It adapts to a chosen writing style and to the content category, and it can carry text straight into translation. Instead of relying on one model, it orchestrates several large language models (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, and LLaMA) and uses a quantitative evaluation step to pick and tune the best output. It runs inside everyday tools such as Word, Notion, and Slack through a keyboard shortcut.
“editorial” is a document-level AI book editor. An editor uploads a full manuscript as PDF, DOCX, HWP, or HWPX, and the system returns a first editing pass in minutes instead of weeks. The pipeline first builds a glossary to check consistency of terms, phrasing, and sentence endings across the whole document. It then proofreads and polishes with the multi-LLM engine, and finally copyedits with fact-checking to catch errors and filter out mis-corrections. Every suggested edit comes with a reason, so a human editor can review and accept it.
Market & Use Cases # BOOKEND serves three groups. Individual editors, authors, and creators use SENTENCIFY on a usage-based SaaS plan. Publishers and content companies use the editing engine through a B2B API. Security-sensitive organizations can run it on-premise.
The clearest use case is speed. A proofreading pass that normally takes weeks can start as a draft in minutes, so editors spend their time on planning and judgment rather than mechanical checks. On-premise delivery fits publishers that cannot send manuscripts to external cloud services. BOOKEND targets Korea and Japan first. Japan is a large publishing market where only sentence-level tools exist today, which leaves room for a document-level AI editor.
Traction & References # BOOKEND has been in the TIPS program since 2023, and early investors include Bluepoint Partners together with the TIPS Program(CB Insights). The company has filed a patent in Korea for its Korean-sentence proofreading technology(CB Insights).
SENTENCIFY is publicly available and supports Korean as its first non-English language, with further languages on its product roadmap. BOOKEND is based at Daejeon Startup Park and is raising a Pre-Series A round(NextUnicorn).
Collaboration Relevance # BOOKEND fits publishers, content companies, and localization or translation firms that handle large volumes of text. The strongest PoC is automated proofreading and copyediting, measured against a publisher’s own manuscripts and house style. On-premise deployment makes it a candidate for security-sensitive publishers and public institutions.
For market entry, Japan is the most direct opportunity because document-level AI editing is not yet served there. For Korea-Europe collaboration, the multi-LLM proofreading engine could extend to European languages, which would make BOOKEND relevant to European publishers, educational-content providers, and content platforms that need consistent, explainable editing at scale.

name: Chingoohaja
summary: Chingoohaja combines senior social connection with AI-based care monitoring.
content:
Company Overview # Chingoohaja develops an AI-based care monitoring platform connecting seniors, families, and care institutions. Addressing challenges in aging societies, the platform enables emotional well-being checks, early detection of cognitive or physical risks through daily speech analysis, and real-time alerts.
Technology & Product # Chingoohaja operates “Mohani,” an interest-based conversation and matching service. The company is also developing AI phone monitoring that analyzes speech, emotion, and conversation patterns.
The system can help detect possible changes in cognitive or emotional state. This gives families and care organizations an additional signal without requiring constant in-person monitoring.
Market & Use Cases # The main users are seniors, families, care organizations, hospitals, telecom companies, and insurers. Use cases include regular check-ins, emotional-care programs, early warning signals, and community-based senior support.
Climate resilience is also relevant. During heat waves or other climate-related risks, remote check-ins can help identify seniors who may need support.
Traction & References # Successfully completed MVP testing and private beta trials based on extensive insights from 250+ senior and caregiver interviews. Received startup support funding and was honored with the National Assembly Speaker Award. Formed collaborative networks with leading institutions, including Seoul AI Hub, Ulsan CCEI, and Samsung Medical Center. Collaboration Relevance # Chingoohaja can work with healthcare providers, senior-care organizations, telecom operators, insurers, and local governments. A useful PoC would test phone-based monitoring with a defined senior group and compare alerts with caregiver feedback.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, the company may fit aging-care innovation, remote care, and climate-risk support for vulnerable groups.

name: Closer Labs
summary: Closer Labs operates Deskroom, an enterprise AI platform for data integration, analytics, and decision support.
content:
Company Overview # Closer Labs operates Deskroom, an enterprise AI platform for business data integration and decision support. The platform connects scattered internal and external data, then helps teams search, analyze, report, and detect issues.
The company started from customer experience and VoC analysis, then expanded Deskroom into a wider AI decision platform for company-wide operations.
Technology & Product # Deskroom connects databases, ERP, CRM, commerce data, advertising data, and external feeds. It uses ontology-based rules so AI can understand business sources, objects, properties, and metrics.
The platform supports natural-language search, dashboard generation, repeated report automation, and anomaly alerts without requiring every user to write SQL.
Market & Use Cases # Closer Labs is relevant for enterprises with many data sources and repeated reporting work. Target teams include operations, customer experience, commerce, marketing, strategy, and management teams.
Use cases include customer inquiry analysis, order and review analysis, business dashboard automation, cross-system search, and data-driven decision support.
Traction & References # Deskroom’s customer cases include CLASS101 and Sentbe. The CLASS101 case includes a 50 percent reduction in refund-related VoC.
Closer Labs signed a Deskroom supply contract with APR in 2025. The company also supplied Deskroom to Ignis for order, review, customer inquiry, SNS, and external brand data analysis.
Deskroom was rebuilt as an AI platform for enterprise decision-making in 2025.
Collaboration Relevance # Closer Labs can work with enterprises that need data integration, AI reporting, and operational decision support. A useful PoC can connect a limited set of CRM, commerce, and customer-service data and test whether teams can reduce manual analysis work.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, the company may fit enterprise AI adoption, cross-border customer operations, and data workflow automation.

name: Daedong Industrial
summary: Daedong Industrial is a Korean automotive plastic-injection manufacturer that also developed BCS, a bio-based carbon-storage permeable paving block.
content:
Company Overview # Daedong Industrial is a Korean manufacturer founded in 2018 and based in Asan, South Chungcheong. Its established business is plastic injection molding and the assembly of automotive interior parts for Hyundai and Kia supply chains, along with some electronic components.
In 2025 the company developed a new product line called BCS (Bio-based Carbon Storage), an eco-friendly permeable paving block. Daedong is now looking for European partners to validate, license, and produce this material locally.
Technology & Product # Automotive plastic parts (core): Injection molding and assembly of interior parts such as console lamp components, armrest boards, cup holders, and trays, supplied into Hyundai and Kia model programs. Electronic components: Injection parts including Smart IC Reels for electronics customers. BCS (Bio-based Carbon Storage) permeable block: An eco-friendly permeable sidewalk block (BCS Block, Permeable 60T, 100 × 200 × 60 mm) that stores carbon in its material structure by replacing virgin raw materials. Compared with cement-based blocks, it adds rainwater infiltration and groundwater recharge, reduces urban surface runoff, and releases heat faster to lessen the heat-island effect. Market & Use Cases # Daedong’s automotive parts serve Hyundai and Kia model programs through Tier suppliers such as Placo, Daeju Precision, Hyundai Industrial, and ITW Automotive Korea. This side of the business is a stable, revenue-generating manufacturing base.
The BCS block targets a different market: municipalities, construction-material manufacturers, paving-block suppliers, and low-carbon building projects that need permeable, carbon-storing pavement. Practical pilot settings include pedestrian paths, green infrastructure, and urban areas exposed to heavy rainfall or heat-island effects.
Traction & References # Daedong supplies injection-molded automotive interior parts for Hyundai and Kia model programs, with assembly and mass-production lines registered with Tier suppliers including ITW Automotive Korea. It holds a Korean patent for its eco-friendly permeable pavement block (KR 10-2996164), registered in 2026. The BCS Permeable 60T block carries a Korean Environmental Product Declaration (EPD), valid 26 Jan 2026 – 25 Jan 2029, with a measured footprint of about 0.730 kg CO₂-eq per block. The company moved into its own factory in Asan in 2024. Collaboration Relevance # For the BCS product, Daedong prefers local production, licensing, technology cooperation, or joint market validation over export alone, given the weight and carbon footprint of construction materials. Relevant partners include European construction-material manufacturers, paving-block suppliers, building-materials and DIY distributors, circular-construction firms, municipalities for pilot sites, and research institutes for EU LCA and EN/DIN standards work.
A pilot could start with a joint review of test reports and a small municipal demo site, then move toward licensed local production. The company also sees joint-development potential in interior finishing, farm trays, buoys, and bicycle or motorbike parts. For Korea-Europe collaboration, the BCS block fits EU priorities on urban water management, climate adaptation, and low-carbon construction materials.

name: Datasketchers
summary: Datasketchers builds AI tools that help suppliers manage ESG and compliance requirements.
content:
Company Overview # Data Sketchers develops AI-driven compliance and ESG management software for global supply chains. The platform automates complex document verification, aligning supplier safety and sustainability data with global buyer standards and food regulatory frameworks, significantly reducing administrative risks and audit times.
Technology & Product # Datasketchers uses RAG-based AI to match supplier audit data with regulations, ESG frameworks, and buyer standards. The system finds compliance gaps and turns them into practical reports.
The company also operates D-SKET services such as web builders, canvas tools, and event support. These services give the team delivery experience with business users and digital workflows.
Market & Use Cases # The main use case is supplier ESG and compliance work in food and FMCG supply chains. Enterprise teams can use the tool to review supplier documents, identify risk, and prepare audit responses faster.
It is also relevant for SMEs that need to meet buyer requirements but do not have a large ESG or legal team.
Traction & References # Datasketchers has venture certification, a company research institute, software business registration, and public procurement vendor status. The company has joined several government support programs and has more than 15 customers.
The company has also received financing support through a direct loan and guarantee program. SK AX and Paradise Group vendor certification are part of its business proof points.
Collaboration Relevance # Datasketchers can work with enterprise procurement teams, ESG teams, food and FMCG brands, and consulting firms. A useful PoC would test whether the AI can reduce review time for supplier documents and create clear compliance reports.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, the company is relevant to supply-chain ESG, food safety, and buyer-driven compliance work.

name: DaWinKS
summary: DaWinKS connects fiat currency and digital assets through MTM/DTM terminals, e-KYC, and blockchain payment infrastructure.
content:
Company Overview # DaWinKS is a South Korean fintech company that connects fiat currency, digital assets, identity verification, and retail payments. Its DPEC Platform links MTM/DTM terminals, crypto POS and QR payment tools, and identity-document scanners. The company began with patent-based scanner supply in 2005 and later expanded into blockchain financial infrastructure.

Its MTM/DTM terminals can combine foreign-currency exchange and digital-asset conversion with services such as prepaid transportation-card issuance, tax refunds, and overseas remittance.

name: DAY1LAB
summary: Alternative plastic materials company developing starch-based biodegradable and microplastic-free materials.
content:
Company Overview # DAY1LAB develops biodegradable plastic alternatives based on starch and other plant-derived natural polymers. Its materials aim to reduce plastic waste, microplastics, and carbon emissions while still working with practical production needs.
The company focuses on a plastic-free material shift. It targets packaging and consumer products that need alternatives to petroleum-based plastic. Its materials are designed to break down in soil, marine, composting, and other controlled environments.
Technology & Product # DAY1LAB’s core material is RETARCH, a thermoplastic starch-based natural polymer that degrades without generating microplastics. The company works from base materials to production-ready compounds and finished products.
Key product and technology areas include:
RETARCH resin grade: a 100% biobased starch-based composite material used as base resin or additive. RETARCH compound grade: production-grade pellets optimized for manufacturing processes. High-barrier coating and film materials: film materials that block oxygen and moisture for food packaging. Final products: finished goods produced on conventional manufacturing lines, including blown film extrusion, T-die extrusion, and injection molding. Market & Use Cases # DAY1LAB is relevant to food packaging companies, consumer goods brands, converters, retailers, and manufacturers. These customers need plastic alternatives that can work with existing production lines.
The company focuses on low-carbon materials, microplastic-free degradation, and compatibility with composting, anaerobic digestion, soil, and marine environments. Near-term applications include packaging, food containers, films, and brand-led plastic reduction programs.
Traction & References # DAY1LAB has raised Series A funding. Cumulative investment is more than KRW 4 billion. DAY1LAB was selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups TIPS program. Certifications include USDA Biobased, TÜV AUSTRIA OK COMPOST HOME/INDUSTRIAL, BPI commercial compostability, Korean environmental labels, ISO 9001, and ISO 14001. DAY1LAB won a CES 2024 Innovation Award in the Sustainability & Energy Transition category. The company also has test data and IP around microplastic-free materials, hazardous-substance safety, green technology, and anaerobic digestion. Collaboration Relevance # Consumer goods brands, retailers, and packaging companies can test DAY1LAB materials for plastic reduction, compostability, and microplastic-free products. Materials companies, compounders, and converters can work with DAY1LAB on formulation, coating, film, and production scale-up. European partners can use DAY1LAB materials where packaging rules, sustainability claims, and material certifications matter.

name: Dynamic Industry
summary: Eco-friendly mechanical recycling systems for recovering valuable materials from end-of-life solar panels.
content:
Company Overview # Dynamic Industry builds physical, eco-friendly recycling systems for decommissioned solar panels. Its equipment dismantles, crushes, and separates panels to recover high-purity glass, aluminum, silicon, silver, and copper. The process uses no toxic chemicals and no high-temperature incineration.
Technology & Product # Dynamic Industry offers physical solar panel recycling systems:
Dismantling & Glass Separation: Machinery automates the removal of aluminum frames and junction boxes, followed by glass separation. Mechanical Sorting: Separation lines crush and sort panel materials using physical forces, such as vibration and gravity density sorting, to isolate valuable metals. Material Recovery: The system recovers key materials such as silicon, glass, aluminum, silver, and copper. Reclaimed metals are refined to industrial grades for reuse in manufacturing. Market & Use Cases # The company works with solar park operators, utility providers, recycling facilities, and waste management companies. By using physical sorting instead of chemical leaching, the system lowers carbon emissions and helps operators meet electronic waste regulations.
Traction & References # Dynamic Industry’s recycling process achieves a material recovery rate of over 90% from decommissioned solar panels. The company was selected for the TIPS research program by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups in July 2024, following seed investment from MYSC in December 2023. The company is a member of the IBK Changgong Daejeon 6th cohort (2024) and was selected for the IBK Changgong Germany 4th cohort in 2025. Dynamic Industry is preparing to export its automated recycling stations to global markets, including the U.S., Germany, Australia, Canada, India, and Vietnam. Collaboration Relevance # Solar farm developers and utility providers can run pilot programs to process retired panels and establish local closed-loop material supply chains. Waste recycling companies in Europe and North America can license or purchase Dynamic Industry’s physical separation equipment to set up localized solar recycling centers. Government environmental agencies and ESG coordinators can work with Dynamic Industry to test chemical-free recycling compliance models in different jurisdictions.

name: E material LAB
summary: Deep-tech developer of passive radiative-cooling components that replace aluminum heat sinks with a lightweight nano-coated material.
content:
Company Overview # E material LAB, Inc. (EML) is a leading-tech startup specializing in next-generation thermal management solutions that overcome the physical limitations of conventional cooling. The company develops high-emissivity passive cooling components designed to replace traditional, bulky aluminum heat sinks.
At the core of its innovation is BLACK metal™, a functional metal sheet featuring a nano-porous layer that dramatically enhances thermal radiation. By maximizing radiation efficiency, EML’s flagship component, HEAT suppressor™, enables heat-generating electronics to be significantly lighter, thinner, and structurally flexible while delivering superior cooling performance.
Aligned with its “Beyond Thermal Limits” mission, EML integrates its cutting-edge material science with sustainable “Green Metal” strategies, reducing carbon emissions throughout the product lifecycle. The company actively targets high-heat industries that drive modern technological evolution, including semiconductors, electric vehicle (EV) components, data centers, mobile devices, and robotics.
Technology & Product # The core innovation relies on BLACK metal™, a highly emissive, functional metal sheet created through a heterojunction process that forms a high-performance radiation layer on aluminum alloy plates. Built on this proprietary material, the HEAT suppressor™ is a next-generation passive cooling component designed to replace conventional, bulky aluminum heat sinks. By fusing advanced material science with micro-geometry, this technology overcomes thermal bottlenecks by maximizing radiation efficiency.
EML achieves a certified emissivity of 0.98 (Double-Radiation-Cooling® Technology); specifically, the BLACK metal™ sheet delivers a 250% increase in heat dissipation performance compared to conventional aluminum plates, while the finished HEAT suppressor™ component provides an average 120% performance level compared to bulky aluminum heat sinks, all while cutting volume and weight by up to 50%. Additionally, its excellent surface electrical insulation completely eliminates the risk of short circuits within high-density electronic environments.
The HEAT suppressor™ offers exceptional forming flexibility; it can be freely pressed and shaped like origami after the thin film layer is applied. To maximize design versatility, it is supplied in three optimized product lineups:
Structured Bodied HEAT suppressor™ (SBH): Rigid, pre-formed structures engineered to replace standard heatsinks for semiconductors and networking housings. Flexible Bodied HEAT suppressor™ (FBH): Thin, sheet-type configurations designed to conform seamlessly to curved, flexible, or highly restricted spaces. Add-on Parts (AOP): Modular, targeted cooling parts designed to be attached directly to specific high-temperature hot spots. These diverse forms enable EML to supply highly tailored solutions—ranging from standard component lineups to customized shapes for electric vehicle (EV) inverters, converters, and robotics.
Market & Use Cases # EML focuses on high-performance industries where excessive heat generation constrains technical progress and device miniaturization. Its core markets include integrated circuits for consumer electronics (Displays, LEDs, home appliances), automotive mobility (EV converters, SiC/GaN-based inverters, battery packs, ADAS systems), computing infrastructure (AI data centers, server racks, GPUs, CPUs), energy storage systems (ESS, battery modules, power conditioning units), and robotics. The HEAT Suppressor™ delivers high-efficiency passive cooling without external power, making it uniquely suited for sealed or space-constrained environments—such as humanoid robot actuators—where conventional bulky heat sinks and fans are impractical. The company commercializes its technology globally through a diversified multi-track business model:
Raw Material Supply: Delivering custom-engineered functional metal coils and sheets to strategic global partners and distributors. Direct Component Delivery: Supplying finished standard and custom-shaped HEAT suppressor™ components directly to Tier-1 manufacturers and OEMs. IP Licensing: Partnering through joint ventures (JVs) to scale its BLACK metal™ technology across international markets while minimizing fixed-cost risks. Traction & References # Recognized for its disruptive deep-tech expertise, EML was selected for Korea’s prestigious TIPS programs in both 2025 and 2026. Supported by the Chungnam Center for Creative Economy and Innovation and the Goyang Industry Promotion Agency, the company has secured critical seed funding alongside extensive government R&D support. Its technological portfolio includes six registered domestic patents, four pending applications, two technology transfers, and two international PCT filings. Further validating its innovation, EML has received the Minister of SMEs and Startups Award and rigorous certification reports from leading national institutes—most notably the Korea Automotive Technology Institute (KATECH)—confirming compliance with stringent automotive AEC-Q standards.
Collaboration Relevance # EML is the ideal partner for semiconductor, electronics, and automotive OEMs seeking to resolve severe thermal bottlenecks without compromising on device weight, thickness, or structural complexity. The company offers versatile collaboration pathways—ranging from raw functional metal coil and sheet supply to direct delivery of standard/custom-molded HEAT suppressor™ components and strategic joint-venture (JV) IP licensing.
Having established advanced joint R&D pipelines with world-renowned institutions like Germany’s Fraunhofer and Singapore’s A*STAR, the company also co-develops tailored, AI-driven thermal simulation models and performs rigorous localized field testing. This comprehensive engagement model is highly relevant for top-tier global manufacturers designing next-generation, space-constrained hardware—such as AI data center server racks, SiC/GaN-based EV inverters, and humanoid robot actuators.

name: Fabricduct
summary: HVAC startup building fabric duct systems for efficient airflow in farms and industrial sites.
content:
Company Overview # Fabricduct builds fabric duct systems for HVAC(Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) airflow control. Its FlowSox system is used in smart farms, logistics centers, factories, cold storage, and other large spaces.
The company focuses on air distribution, not only HVAC capacity. Better airflow can reduce dead zones, temperature gaps, humidity problems, and energy waste.
Technology & Product # FlowSox is a fabric duct and design platform. Fabricduct designs, makes, installs, and checks ducts for each site.
Core product and service categories include:
FlowSox fabric ducts for cooling, heating, and ventilation. Fabric defrost pockets for cold-chain and refrigeration sites. Laser-hole airflow design and CFD-based design review. Site checks before and after installation. Future FlowSox Builder SaaS for HVAC partners and distributors. Market & Use Cases # Fabricduct is relevant to energy-intensive facilities. Target users include smart farms, vertical farms, food factories, pharmaceutical factories, logistics centers, cold storage sites, data centers, and HVAC contractors.
Use cases include even air distribution, lower HVAC energy waste, better crop or product quality, faster installation, and safer airflow in large rooms.

Grew revenue by 750% after joining the Youth Startup Academy and received the MSS Minister’s Award(InTheNews). Deployed at more than 20 facilities including Kurly, Korea Post, Coupang, Baemin B Mart, and Poongsan(Seoul Economic Daily). Participated in the ClimateLaunchpad program for clean-tech innovations. name: Faddit
summary: Faddit automates fashion production workflows from design sketch to CAD pattern.
content:
Company Overview # Faddit provides a cloud-based SaaS platform that digitalizes fashion design-to-production workflows. By connecting design sketches, technical drawings, patterns, and production orders in a unified workspace, it eliminates communication errors between fashion brands and factories, reducing sample remaking costs and fabric waste.
Technology & Product # Faddit is developing an AI fashion production workflow platform. The system can turn vector sketches into CAD pattern outputs and help prepare tech packs, flats, and production documents.
The product direction also includes 2D and 3D review, fabric selection, and production request workflows. These functions are useful when small brands need to move from idea to sample without a large in-house production team.
Market & Use Cases # Faddit is relevant for independent designers, small fashion brands, pattern makers, and sewing factories. It can support small-batch production, sample development, and digital handoff between design and manufacturing.
The company also connects to the Dongdaemun production ecosystem, where many small factories need clearer digital production data.
Traction & References # Faddit was selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups TIPS program in November 2025.
The company is taking preorders and is building around a network of Dongdaemun sewing factories. The team is using ClimateLaunchpad to connect fashion production automation with lower waste and circular fashion goals.
Collaboration Relevance # Faddit can work with fashion brands, CAD software partners, textile suppliers, sewing factory networks, and sustainability programs. A useful PoC would test whether the software reduces sample-production time and miscommunication between designers and factories.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, Faddit may fit small-batch production, local manufacturing networks, and fashion supply-chain digitization.

name: FUST Lab
summary: Developer of DEBREX focused ultrasonic nano-dispersion equipment for chemical and battery formulations.
content:
Company Overview # FUST Lab is a research-company spinout from the Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science. It builds focused ultrasonic equipment for material processing and wastewater treatment. The technology supports nano-emulsification, dispersion, extraction, and ultrasonic advanced oxidation.
Its main platform, DEBREX, supports surfactant-free nano-dispersion and emulsification. It is useful for materials that are hard to process with standard equipment. FUST Lab also develops CAVITOX for difficult industrial and pharmaceutical wastewater, including PFAS-related use cases.
Technology & Product # FUST Lab has product lines for material processing and water treatment:
DEBREX: focused ultrasonic equipment for emulsification, dispersion, extraction, and water treatment. DEBREX 30/50 are for formulation R&D, DEBREX 100 is for continuous processing, and DEBREX 500 is for scale-up and mass production. CAVITOX: ultrasonic advanced oxidation equipment for hard-to-degrade wastewater, including PFAS-related contaminants. Cosmetics ODM: surfactant-free cosmetic formulation and ODM using DEBREX process technology. FUST Lab also built a demo-room setup in Germany for European customer testing. DEBREX uses cylindrical ultrasonic processing to focus energy inside a controlled flow path. Cooling, real-time frequency tracking, flow-rate control, automated cleaning, and monitoring help stable operation from lab tests to production.
Relevant materials include SWCNT, MXene, carbon nanomaterials, nickel and metal powders, battery materials, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, specialty chemicals, and electronic materials.

name: GIGR
summary: GIGR builds Playad, a multi-agent AI platform that plans, creates, tests, and optimizes ad creative.
content:
Company Overview # GIGR is an adtech startup that uses generative AI agents to run the full ad creative workflow. The company is based in San Francisco and has Korean roots. Its first product, Playad, covers planning, production, testing, and performance optimization in one platform.
The goal is to remove the high cost and long lead time of traditional creative production. GIGR focuses on teams that need large volumes of ad creative and fast performance feedback, especially in gaming and commerce.
Technology & Product # Playad is a multi-agent AI platform for marketing creative. It takes campaign performance data, then plans and generates new ad assets such as video, images, and banners. It feeds these assets back into the ad system and learns from the results.
Playad is built as an AI-native creative platform. It started with interactive advertising and expanded to images and video. The product launched in the third quarter of 2025.
Market & Use Cases # The main users are marketing teams with heavy creative production needs. Gaming and commerce are the primary target markets because they require frequent creative refreshes and rapid A/B testing.
Useful settings include user acquisition campaigns, creative scaling for app installs, and performance marketing teams that want to cut production cost while testing more variants.
Traction & References # GIGR raised a USD 5.4 million pre-seed round (about KRW 7.9 billion)(Byline Network). The round was led by BRV Capital Management, with Mirae Asset Venture Investment participating. Angel investors included Krafton outside director Bo-ra Jeong and Hyprsense founder Ji-hoon Yoo(Venture Square).
Some client cases show ad creative production cost falling by up to 90 percent, alongside better user acquisition efficiency(Venture Square). GIGR was selected for the 2026 Gangnam-gu testbed program.
Collaboration Relevance # GIGR fits gaming studios, app publishers, and commerce brands that run high-volume performance marketing. A practical pilot would connect Playad to an existing ad account and measure creative cost and acquisition efficiency against the current workflow.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, GIGR could work with mobile gaming and e-commerce companies that scale paid user acquisition across markets and need localized creative at volume.

name: Globaleur
summary: B2B AI platform that turns traveler data into personalized recommendations for airlines, hotels, and tourism brands.
content:
Company Overview # Globaleur is a B2B AI platform for the travel industry. It helps airlines, hotels, airports, tourism boards, card issuers, and travel platforms turn traveler data into personalized recommendations, commerce actions, and service experiences.
The company started in Silicon Valley in 2017. Its headquarters is in San Francisco, with an R&D team in Seoul.
Technology & Product # Globaleur supplies its AI as software that travel companies can add to their own apps and websites. The platform is built around several capabilities:
AI Travel Concierge — personalized trip planning and recommendations. Destination Intelligence — a large base of destination data covering attractions, hotels, and activities. Commerce Orchestration — connecting recommendations to bookings such as flights, hotels, and local activities. The engine ingests traveler signals like loyalty status, itinerary, and behavior from systems such as PSS, CRM, and PMS. It then returns personalized recommendations across digital touchpoints in under one second.
Market & Use Cases # The main customers are travel enterprises that want to grow revenue on their own channels and depend less on large online travel agencies. Typical buyers are airlines, global hotel chains, airports, tourism boards, and credit card companies.
A clear use case is an airline or hotel adding an AI travel planner to its own app. The platform combines preferences, local weather, and travel conditions to suggest tailored content, then links the trip to bookings in a single flow.
Traction & References # The platform handles 200K+ commerce integrations and a base of 1.5M+ destination vectors, with sub-second decision latency, 99.99% uptime, and support for 15+ languages. Globaleur runs on SOC-2 aligned controls and offers private deployment, data isolation, and encryption for enterprise customers. The company placed second (Top Voted) at the Singapore Airlines AppChallenge 2020. Globaleur was selected as one of the Seoul Tourism Organization’s 2020 tourism startup projects(Seoul Tourism). Globaleur raised a Pre-Series A round of about KRW 3.6 billion, with K-Net Investment Partners and Silicon Valley VCs participating(ET News). Globaleur was selected for the 2026 Gangnam-gu Test Bed program. Collaboration Relevance # Globaleur fits enterprises that want to add AI-driven personalization to their own travel channels without building it in-house. Strong partner types are airlines, hotel groups, airports, tourism boards, and card issuers.
Useful collaboration angles include a PoC that embeds the recommendation engine into an existing app, integration with loyalty and booking systems, and joint go-to-market with travel brands. The US-Korea structure, with a San Francisco HQ and a Seoul R&D team, supports cross-border pilots between the two markets.

name: IOMTEK
summary: Eco-friendly composite materials and climate-responsive films made from waste plastics and industrial by-products.
content:
Company Overview # IOMTEK makes upcycled materials. The company develops composite materials and functional films from waste plastics and industrial by-products. Its durable structural materials and thermal insulation films help lower industrial carbon footprints and support resource circularity.
Technology & Product # IOMTEK offers two primary technology and product categories:
Composite Materials: Upcycled structural materials made from industrial by-products and waste plastic. They offer mechanical durability and cost-efficiency. Applications include aviation, defense, automotive, electronics, and robotics components. Climate-Responsive Films: Durable insulation films made from recycled polymers. They provide thermal insulation, climate resilience, and energy conservation. Market & Use Cases # IOMTEK serves industries that use large volumes of structural polymers and insulation materials: construction, civil engineering, transport, and manufacturing. Key use cases include recycled composite panels, railway sleepers, industrial packaging, and energy-saving building wraps.
Traction & References # IOMTEK was founded in August 2020 as the first corporate spin-off from POSCO’s internal startup incubation program. The company secured Seed investment from POSTECH Holdings in 2020 and follow-on funding from Future Science & Technology Holdings in 2021. IOMTEK was selected for the TIPS startup incubator program in April 2021. The company was selected by the Korea Railroad Research Institute (KRRI) in June 2021 to develop composite railway sleepers. Collaboration Relevance # Civil engineering firms and rail operators can work with IOMTEK to test and deploy upcycled composite sleepers and panels for public infrastructure. Automotive and industrial equipment manufacturers can partner with IOMTEK to prototype composite parts that meet mechanical strength standards. Real estate developers and insulation installers can run PoCs with IOMTEK’s climate-responsive films to improve building thermal performance and earn carbon credits.

name: IPIN LABS
summary: AI-based indoor positioning and asset tracking that works in GPS-denied industrial sites using existing wireless signals.
content:
Company Overview # IPIN LABS provides AI-based indoor positioning and asset tracking for industrial sites where GPS does not work. Its location-based digital-twin solution monitors assets in real time. The approach is infrastructure-free: it uses existing Wi-Fi, BLE, and 5G signals instead of dedicated anchors, and can be deployed within 24 hours.
Technology & Product # BPIN: A location-based asset management solution. It offers asset search, floor-by-floor status, location tracking, heatmaps, movement tracking, and asset management. AI indoor positioning engine: A deep-learning approach that uses a wide range of RF signals rather than a fixed anchor setup, which reduces the cost and setup overhead of BLE/UWB anchor and fingerprinting methods. It pairs this with AI-IMU to simplify walk-based data collection. Market & Use Cases # The main customers are operators of large indoor or mixed indoor-outdoor sites that need to track moving assets. Application examples include construction sites and international airports, where assets and their movement paths are tracked in real time and geofencing helps prevent loss or misplacement. It also fits environments where rental assets such as carts and strollers move between indoor and outdoor zones.
Traction & References # BPIN won a CES 2025 Innovation Award in the industrial equipment and machinery category(IPIN LABS Blog). The company lists SK telecom, SK hynix, and Wistron among its references(IPIN LABS). Total measured area reached about 1.66 million m² as of November 2024(IPIN LABS). At CES 2025, the company held asset-tracking discussions with a US office-supplies distributor, an automaker, and a large Japanese SI firm(IPIN LABS Blog). Collaboration Relevance # Smart-factory, logistics, and construction operators can run PoCs to track tools, equipment, and inventory in GPS-denied indoor sites. System integrators and facility operators can embed BPIN as a real-time location layer in digital-twin platforms. The CES award and overseas business talks show readiness for Korea-Europe market entry through SI or distribution partners.

name: KL Cube
summary: KL Cube provides AI sign-language translation and 3D avatar services for accessible digital and physical customer experiences.
content:
Company Overview # KL Cube is a South Korean AI company that develops digital-accessibility services for Deaf and hard-of-hearing users. Its main platform, HandSignVerse, converts Korean text or speech into Korean Sign Language (KSL) and presents it through 3D avatars.
The service works across websites, mobile apps, kiosks, digital desks, QR-linked pages, and video content. KL Cube also develops AI contact-center software, while its current growth strategy focuses on sign-language and accessibility services.
Technology & Product # HandSignVerse combines Korean-language analysis, sign-language sentence generation, sign-asset retrieval, avatar animation, and content management. Its NOVA engine analyzes text or speech, creates a sign-language sequence with facial and body expressions, selects matching assets, and renders a 3D avatar.
The platform also includes HandSign TalkTalk for information and consultation, QRing for QR-based guidance, SignBot for rule-based conversations, and MindSign for signed meditation and emotional-care content. Organizations can use the platform as on-premise software, SaaS, or a hybrid deployment and connect it to existing services through APIs.
KL Cube has built a Korean-KSL parallel corpus of more than four million eojeol across public administration, healthcare, finance, education, tourism, shopping, news, and daily-life domains. Specialist reviewers check translations before release.
Market & Use Cases # KL Cube serves public agencies, hospitals, banks, insurers, transport operators, tourism organizations, libraries, schools, and consumer-service companies. These organizations can add sign-language guidance without building their own translation, avatar, and review workflow.
Typical uses include accessible ticketing and information kiosks, mobile banking guidance, hospital navigation, signed food information linked by QR codes, museum and tourism content, digital sign-language books, and guidance on smart devices.
Traction & References # KL Cube has deployed a hospital information kiosk at Korea University Anam Hospital, a museum guide at Dasan Art Museum, and sign-language content for the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family’s child-care portal(KL Cube product page). It works with public, healthcare, finance, and technology organizations including Namyangju City, Catholic University St. Vincent’s Hospital, Food Safety Korea, and Hana Card(KL Cube partners).
HandSign TalkTalk received a CES 2025 Innovation Award and a 2025 Edison Awards Silver award(Edison Awards). KL Cube holds GS Certification Grade 1, a TI-2 technology rating, and CSAP SaaS certification. HandSign TalkTalk was designated an Innovative Product by Korea’s Public Procurement Service, and KL Cube received the 2026 New Software Product Award(KL Cube history). KL Cube holds 11 registered patents and was selected for the 2026 Gangnam-gu Global Testbed program.
Collaboration Relevance # Banks, hospitals, public agencies, transport operators, and tourism businesses can add HandSignVerse to an existing app, website, kiosk, or customer desk. A focused PoC can test translation quality, user comprehension, response time, and operational workload for one service journey.
Device makers can license the platform for kiosks, vehicles, appliances, tablets, and digital desks. For Korea-Europe expansion, KL Cube can work with local sign-language experts, accessibility organizations, and distribution partners to build country-specific language assets and meet local accessibility requirements.

name: Klio Design
summary: Design studio helping companies build mobility, product, and service experiences.
content:
Company Overview # Klio Design is a global design studio specializing in future mobility, digital user experience (UX), product design, and brand styling. Based on the philosophy of “Design for Living,” the studio crafts intuitive design solutions that seamlessly integrate technology into daily life.
The studio serves as an essential design partner for startups and R&D organizations, transforming complex hardware, mobility, and sustainability technologies into user-friendly products and clear visual communications.
Technology & Product # Klio Design works across design strategy, mobility design, product design, service design, UX/UI, CMF, and brand experience. Its work covers both physical products and digital touchpoints.
Rather than just offering cosmetic design support, Klio Design provides comprehensive execution capabilities—ranging from user research and CMF (Color, Materials, Finish) strategy to physical prototyping and interface design.
Key design expertise includes:
Mobility and future vehicle experience design. Product and device design. Service and UX design. Brand and communication design. Sustainable product and experience concepts. Market & Use Cases # Klio Design is relevant to startups, corporates, and R&D teams that need to make a technology easier to understand, test, and commercialize. This is especially useful for hardware, mobility, consumer product, and sustainability projects.
Typical use cases include concept design for new products, mobility interior or interface concepts, product-service experience design, pitch-ready visual communication, prototype design, and market-entry design localization.
Traction & References # Built a solid track record of collaborative R&D design projects with major automotive OEMs and technology groups. Established Klio Design Europe Studio in Munich, Germany, facilitating design localization and European partner collaborations. Executed multiple high-profile projects in future mobility interior concept design, consumer device styling, and sustainable materials experience design. Collaboration Relevance # Technology startups can work with Klio Design to turn early product ideas into user-ready concepts, prototypes, and pitch materials. Mobility, hardware, and sustainability teams can use Klio Design for PoCs where design quality affects user adoption, partner buy-in, or investor understanding. Korea-Europe projects can use Klio Design’s design studio capability and European presence for market-entry design, localization, and customer-facing communication.

content:
Company Overview # Linetron develops software solutions for automotive software testing and validation, with a focus on automating the increasingly complex verification requirements of Software-Defined Vehicles.
Technology & Product # Its core solution, AutoTest, is an AI-based test automation platform for vehicle and functional-safety ECU software. The system automatically generates test scenarios based on ECU function specifications, operating conditions, and simulation data, then executes and analyzes repeated verification tests.
By automating regression testing, AutoTest addresses the growing testing workload associated with frequent software updates and OTA deployments.
Market & Use Cases # The technology can support SDV software validation, ECU testing, functional-safety verification, regression testing, and OTA software development. It is designed to work with established automotive testing environments and tools, including dSPACE, Vector, and ETAS.
Traction & References # Linetron brings more than 20 years of automotive software experience. Its technology can reduce test preparation time from months to weeks and automate repetitive testing across the software validation cycle. The core solution is currently at approximately TRL 5, with further development toward TRL 7 for real-world deployment.
Collaboration Relevance # For Mercedes-Benz, Linetron’s AutoTest could support faster validation of MB.OS and vehicle software updates by automatically generating, executing, and analyzing test scenarios. This could help reduce manual testing workload as software complexity and OTA update frequency increase.

name: LMNTIC Biotech
summary: A single-chip platform that uses a magnetic field to pull cancer cells out of a blood sample, then reads their DNA for cancer diagnostics.
content:
Company Overview # LMNTIC Biotech is a cancer diagnostics company. Its technology isolates circulating tumor cells (CTCs) — cancer cells that break off a tumor and travel in the bloodstream — from a blood sample. Founded in 2022, the company is based at DGIST (a research university in Korea) and builds on magnetophoretic cell-control technology developed by Prof. Cheol-Gi Kim at DGIST. The goal is to make liquid biopsy — a cancer test that uses a blood sample instead of surgically removing tissue — faster, cheaper, and easier to access than a tissue biopsy.
Technology & Product # The core product is L:Biopsy, an automated platform built around a single microfluidic chip. It tags the target cells with magnetic particles and then uses a magnetic field to move and sort them one cell at a time — a technique called micro-magnetophoresis. In one automated run from 10 mL of blood, it captures the tumor cells, images them, and recovers about 87% of them while removing nearly all normal blood cells; a high-purity mode is designed to reach over 90% purity for sequencing. The captured cells can then go into genomic sequencing — reading their DNA to spot mutations and possible treatment targets. The run takes about four hours, needs no centrifuge, and uses a benchtop device that costs a fraction of existing CTC-isolation systems.
Market & Use Cases # The platform is built for research labs, hospitals, and cancer centers that need a reliable way to isolate CTCs. They use it to count and characterize tumor cells, track how a patient responds to treatment, and support research that moves lab findings toward the clinic. It is positioned as a lower-cost option and can be used alongside tissue biopsies and ctDNA tests (which look for tumor DNA in the blood). For now it is a research-use-only tool, so it fits early-stage cancer studies and biomarker work rather than routine clinical care.
Traction & References # LMNTIC was selected for TIPS in 2022 and completed seed funding the same year, with a lab-startup grant and follow-on investment reported afterward(Hankyung). The company joined the IBK Changgong Guro 13th cohort(Hankyung). It won an Excellence Award at the 2025 Science and Technology Specialized University startup investment competition run with KAIST, GIST, DGIST, UNIST, POSTECH, and KDB(ETNews). Founder Donghwan Ryu was named to the Forbes Korea 30 Under 30 list in 2025(Forbes Korea). The company also runs joint R&D with the Seoul St. Mary’s Hospital Bio Core Facility and holds Korean venture company certification and a corporate research institute(LMNTIC).
Collaboration Relevance # LMNTIC is a good match for cancer centers and research groups that need very pure CTC samples to validate their work in patients. Its roots at DGIST and its ongoing hospital partnership open clear paths for joint studies. For drug companies, the platform can help build companion diagnostics (CDx) — tests that help pick the right targeted therapy for a patient — and co-develop CTC-based markers, which fits the company’s stated interest in research and CDx partnerships.

name: Lymeric
summary: AI and physics-based platform that predicts material properties to speed up materials R&D.
content:
Company Overview # Lymeric builds AI software for materials research and development. The platform predicts material properties so R&D teams can find good candidates faster and rely less on costly lab experiments.
The company combines machine learning, computational chemistry, and accumulated experimental data. This helps researchers work in fields where data is scarce or testing is expensive, such as batteries, displays, and semiconductors.
Technology & Product # The core approach is physics-informed AI. By adding physical rules to the models, Lymeric can predict reliable property values even with a small amount of experimental data.
The platform is built as a set of modules for materials R&D:
Physics-informed property prediction. Candidate screening to narrow down promising compositions. A Sim-to-Lab workflow that connects simulation results to real lab validation. This lets a research team move from molecular and nanoscale analysis to experimental checks within one connected environment.
Market & Use Cases # The main users are corporate and institutional materials R&D teams. Typical use cases include predicting and optimizing new compositions for battery cathode and anode materials, and predicting blended formulations for cosmetics active ingredients.
The platform fits research areas where each experiment is slow and expensive. In these fields, better candidate prediction directly cuts development time and cost.
Traction & References # The company was selected for the 2026 Gangnam-gu Test Bed program. Lymeric is selectively discussing pilot projects and partnerships with materials R&D teams(Lymeric). Collaboration Relevance # Lymeric is a good fit for joint pilots with companies that run materials R&D and want to reduce experiment cycles. Strong partner types include battery, display, semiconductor, and cosmetics R&D teams.
Useful collaboration angles include a focused PoC on one material class, integration of the prediction modules into an existing R&D workflow, and data partnerships where a company’s experimental data improves model accuracy. As an early-stage company, Lymeric is most relevant for early technology validation rather than large-scale deployment today.
