name: Vision Innovation
summary: Vision Innovation develops functional injection-molding nozzle solutions that enable manufacturers to increase the use of recycled plastics in automotive components.
content:
Company Overview # Vision Innovation develops functional injection-molding nozzle solutions that enable manufacturers to increase the use of recycled plastics in automotive components. Its technology focuses on removing gases, moisture, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released by recycled resins during the injection-molding process, helping improve product quality while reducing energy consumption and manufacturing costs.
Technology & Product # Its core solution, Vision Nozzle, is a multi-type functional nozzle available in pin-type and screw-type configurations. Installed directly at the injection stage, the nozzle removes gases, moisture, and VOCs from recycled resin immediately before injection. Combined with a dedicated controller and AI-based process data analysis, the system aims to replace conventional pre-drying processes without requiring modifications to existing injection-molding machines.
By reducing drying time and improving process stability, Vision Nozzle enables manufacturers to increase recycled plastic content while maintaining consistent molding quality.
Market & Use Cases # The technology can support automotive interior and exterior plastic components, recycled plastic processing, injection-molding process optimization, VOC reduction, and sustainable manufacturing. Potential applications include increasing post-consumer recycled (PCR) and post-industrial recycled (PIR) material content in automotive supplier production lines, while reducing defects, drying energy consumption, and material waste.
Traction & References # Vision Innovation has validated its technology at five sites in Korea and overseas, reporting a reduction in defect rates from 4.7% to 1.1% and an increase in production output by approximately 1.8 times. Testing witnessed by KTR demonstrated CO gas removal exceeding 30%, reaching approximately 40% under specified PP+GF30 conditions. The company also reports that its technology can reduce pre-drying time from 2–8 hours to 0–2 hours and increase recycled material content from approximately 10% to over 30%.
Commercial traction includes an export contract in Vietnam, purchase orders in China, and an MOU in the EU. The core pin-type nozzle is at approximately TRL 6–7, with further development underway for larger-capacity nozzle configurations and AI-based process control.
Collaboration Relevance # For Mercedes-Benz and its automotive supplier network, Vision Innovation’s Vision Nozzle could enable higher recycled-plastic content in injection-molded components while reducing manufacturing defects, drying energy consumption, and material costs. A pilot on existing supplier production lines could help assess its contribution to recycled-material targets, VOC reduction, and the EU End-of-Life Vehicles (ELV) regulatory requirements without requiring major changes to existing equipment.

name: VISIONSPACE
summary: VISIONSPACE builds digital twin and Physical AI software that simulates and monitors factory and logistics automation.
content:
Company Overview # VISIONSPACE builds digital twin and Physical AI software for factory and logistics automation. The platform turns a real site into a virtual model, then uses AI simulation and real-time 3D monitoring to design and run automation. The company describes its tools as an all-in-one digital twin solution that supports projects from planning to operation.
The company was founded in 2023 and is based in Seongnam, with a Seoul branch. Its two core products are TESSERACT and TARS.
Technology & Product # TESSERACT is a Physical AI robot simulator built on digital twin technology. It designs and tests space layout, robot placement, equipment flow, and operating scenarios in a virtual environment. Its own engine can generate a 3D simulation from drawings and images alone, which lets teams validate an automation plan before going live. The product page reports up to 23 percent lower development and operating cost, around 30 percent OEE improvement, up to 25 percent shorter cycle time, and up to 80 percent fewer delays or failures.
TARS is a low-latency AI control system that links robots, equipment, and existing systems. It moves beyond simple monitoring to AI-based autonomous control and integrated management, with real-time 3D monitoring of the whole site. The platform also includes an AI 3D generator and a DB engine that connects to a customer’s existing APIs for real-time data collection and analysis.
Market & Use Cases # VISIONSPACE targets manufacturers and logistics operators that plan or run automated facilities. It fits warehouse automation, smart factories, and any site that wants to test a robot and equipment layout before investing.
Practical use cases include designing a new automated warehouse, validating robot work paths, and running an integrated control room for mixed equipment and robots.
Traction & References # VISIONSPACE raised a pre-seed round from 500 Global, announced in January 2025(BusinessKorea). It was selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups Deep-Tech TIPS program in November 2024, and won the top innovation award in the ABB category at the FIX 2024 Innovation Awards(FIX Korea).
On the commercial side, the company signed digital twin contracts in 2025 with Hyundai Movex for the Cheongna logistics center and with LX (Korea Land and Geospatial Informatix) for the new Dongjak-gu building. It was also selected for IBK Changgong’s Silicon Valley 2nd cohort(Asia Economy) and joined global events including MWC 2025 and VIVA Technology Paris.
Collaboration Relevance # VISIONSPACE fits logistics operators, manufacturers, system integrators, and robot vendors. A practical pilot would model one real warehouse or production line, then compare simulated layouts against current operations on cost, cycle time, and throughput.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, its work at MWC and VIVA Technology and its automation focus make it relevant to European manufacturing and logistics partners exploring digital twin and Physical AI deployment.

name: VSION
summary: VSION develops switchable smart-glass materials for automotive applications, with a focus on privacy, thermal management, energy efficiency, and premium vehicle design.
content:
Company Overview # VSION develops switchable smart-glass materials for automotive applications, with a focus on privacy, thermal management, energy efficiency, and premium vehicle design.
Technology & Product # Its key technology is a transmittance-variable black PDLC film for automotive roof glass. The film appears opaque black when the power is off and becomes transparent when activated.
Compared with conventional white or milky PDLC films, the technology provides a darker premium appearance while also helping block UV radiation and solar heat. This can improve occupant privacy and potentially reduce cooling loads inside the vehicle.
Market & Use Cases # The technology is particularly suited to automotive roof glass, panoramic roofs, privacy glass, and premium vehicle interiors. It can also be applied to architectural, rail, and aviation glazing.
Traction & References # VSION operates its own materials and production capabilities, with a reported 90%+ production yield. Its technology is currently being evaluated through PoCs with major glass manufacturers including Saint-Gobain and Asahi and has applications across building, rail, and aviation sectors. The technology is currently assessed at approximately TRL 5–6, with samples undergoing reliability evaluation.
Collaboration Relevance # For Mercedes-Benz, VSION could support the development of a switchable black smart-glass roof option, providing on-demand privacy, solar and heat control, and a premium visual experience. Potential collaboration could focus on automotive validation and eventual OEM supply.

name: VTouch
summary: Deep-tech developer of natural user interfaces — contactless spatial touch, voice-AI wearables, and mid-air hologram controls.
content:
Company Overview # VTouch is a Korean deep-tech company that builds natural user interfaces for computing without screens or physical buttons. It is based in Seocho-gu, Seoul. The company develops three core interaction methods: contactless spatial touch that lets users control devices by pointing at them, a voice-AI wearable ring, and mid-air hologram buttons. Its goal is to make everyday interaction with devices, cars, and public machines faster and more hygienic by removing the need to touch a surface.
Technology & Product # VTouch’s flagship consumer product is the WIZPR RING, a titanium ring that lets the wearer talk to AI assistants with a quiet whisper. Because the microphone sits close to the mouth, sound pressure at 5 cm is about 100 times higher than at 50 cm, so it works in noisy places and does not need a wake word. Raising the hand to the mouth auto-unlocks voice input, and the ring stops listening when it moves away, which reduces false triggers and protects privacy. A physical button adds hybrid control, including a five-press SOS mode with location sharing. The ring weighs 4 grams and is IPX4 water-resistant. VTouch’s other line, Spatial Touch, lets a user control air vents, windows, speakers, and displays by pointing in mid-air, using a motion-prediction algorithm for near-zero latency and a multi-step filter to prevent accidental input. Holo Button adds contactless control through a floating hologram.
Market & Use Cases # The spatial touch technology targets the automotive industry, especially future autonomous and semi-autonomous vehicles where fixed button layouts no longer fit flexible seating. It also suits shared vehicles and public machines where touchless control improves hygiene. The WIZPR RING targets consumers who want hands-free, discreet access to AI assistants while walking, driving, or working. Hologram controls fit kiosks, elevators, appliances, and product showcases where users prefer not to touch shared surfaces.
Traction & References # VTouch holds about 120 patents in natural user interfaces. It has shown prototypes and technology with major carmakers and electronics firms, including Hyundai Mobis concept cabins and a Kia autonomous-cabin demo at CES 2019. The company has received CES Innovation Awards across several years, including CES 2021, CES 2022, and CES 2024, with the WIZPR RING winning a CES 2024 Innovation Award. The WIZPR RING launched through crowdfunding in March 2024, with a retail price of $199. Co-CEO SeokJoong Kim was named “Invention King of the Year” in 2021.
Collaboration Relevance # VTouch fits carmakers, tier-1 automotive suppliers, and appliance and electronics makers that want touchless or voice control built into their products. It is well suited to PoC and joint development for in-cabin interfaces, hologram kiosks, and voice-AI hardware, and to licensing from its large patent portfolio. For AI and assistant platforms, the WIZPR RING can act as a discreet, always-ready input device. Its Seoul base and existing work with global automotive and electronics partners make it a practical partner for Korea-Europe technology projects.

name: Woozza
summary: Woozza operates an urban disaster-response platform built on high-density rainfall observation and AI flood prediction.
content:
Company Overview # Woozza operates an urban disaster-response platform built on high-density rainfall observation and AI flood prediction. It runs FLOOD WATCH and provides minute-level rainfall data and real-time flood-risk information. It supports early action by public officials and connects sensors, data collection, prediction models, alerts, and evacuation support in one system.
Technology & Product # Its core hardware is a WMO-standard smart rain gauge. Woozza deploys the gauges at much higher density than conventional public weather networks and collects rainfall data every minute. The devices support LTE, 5G, and LoRa wireless communication, with solar-powered field operation.
On top of the sensing layer, Woozza runs an AI-based flood prediction system. It analyzes rainfall data, road water levels, and local risk information to issue early flood forecasts. It also connects care officials, community partners, and vulnerable residents through an evacuation-support workflow.
Market & Use Cases # Its main users are local governments, disaster-response agencies, and public infrastructure operators. The platform supports district-level urban flood management, evacuation support for vulnerable populations, and real-time decision support for public-safety teams.
Woozza also serves power plants, rail facilities, and industrial complexes with high flood risk. The same framework extends into smart-city weather infrastructure, water management, and climate-risk services.
Traction & References # Woozza deploys WMO-standard rain gauges at 13 to 20 times the density of traditional weather observation networks. It uses 1-minute data for real-time flood prediction and alerts. The company has built and operated a real-time rainfall observation network in Gwanak-gu, Seoul, and used it as a reference site for district-level flood monitoring and response operations. Its operating model includes a disaster-response workflow for vulnerable households in Seoul, including flood forecast thresholds, alert routing, and evacuation support coordination for care officials and community partners. The company has validated its AI flood prediction model for power-plant flooding response use cases. It is advancing rainfall observation and flood prediction technology with Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology (KICT). Woozza has also run joint validation with Thuy Loi University in Vietnam and pursued market validation for flood-response solutions in the United States. Revenue reached KRW 540 million in 2025. Collaboration Relevance # Woozza is a practical PoC partner for cities, utilities, and infrastructure operators that need localized rainfall intelligence instead of coarse regional weather feeds. A project can start with dense sensor deployment in one district or facility. It can then extend into prediction dashboards, alert workflows, and response automation.
Woozza also fits climate adaptation, smart-city infrastructure, and public-safety data projects. Its references span municipal flood operations, vulnerable-population evacuation support, industrial flooding use cases, and international validation. That mix makes it a credible partner for cross-border disaster-tech pilots.

name: YGGR
summary: An F&B company that runs the premium Greek yogurt brand Lazy Yogurt, with 72-hour whey straining and its own manufacturing facility.
content:
Company Overview # Lazy Yogurt is a premium Greek yogurt brand operated by YGGR Corp. (WG&R Co., Ltd.). The brand strains whey slowly over 72 hours to produce a thick, high-protein yogurt made with grade-1 raw milk and probiotic cultures.
The parent company develops and runs consumer F&B brands. Alongside Lazy Yogurt, it operates the FOROOTS influencer marketing platform and a Japan-focused curation media brand, building a portfolio that links product manufacturing with brand and marketing channels.
Technology & Product # The core product is Lazy Yogurt Greek yogurt. The 72-hour whey straining process raises protein concentration and creates a dense, chewy texture. The recipe uses no preservatives or artificial colors and offers plain, flavored, and pet-friendly lines.
The company manufactures in its own facility in Seongsu-dong, Seoul, which supports volume production and retail distribution. It also runs FOROOTS, an in-house influencer marketing platform used to support brand growth in Korea and overseas.
Market & Use Cases # The main customers are health-conscious consumers who want high-protein, clean-label yogurt. Lazy Yogurt sells through its own stores, e-commerce, and a Naver Smart Store, and supports group catering and B2B partnership programs.
The brand is also relevant for retail and franchise expansion, both in Korea and in overseas markets that have growing demand for premium Greek yogurt.
Traction & References # Lazy Yogurt operates four physical stores, including two in Osaka, Japan (Namba and Nakazakicho), in addition to its Seoul locations(Lazy Yogurt). The company is pursuing a master franchise structure to expand the brand in the Japanese market.
The company built its own manufacturing facility in Seongsu-dong and obtained HACCP food-safety certification. It received seed investment from accelerator KingoSpring(EnetNews). It was also selected for the 2026 Gangnam-gu Test-Bed program.
Collaboration Relevance # YGGR can work with retailers, franchise partners, and food distributors that want a differentiated premium yogurt brand. Its in-house manufacturing and marketing platform make it a candidate for co-branding, private-label production, and overseas market entry.
For Korea-Europe collaboration, the brand is relevant to premium dairy retail, clean-label F&B distribution, and franchise or import partnerships built on its own production capability.

name: Zephyros Electronic
summary: Zephyros Electronic develops software solutions for electronic design automation (EDA), specializing in automated PCB filter design and electromagnetic simulation.
content:
Company Overview # Zephyros Electronic develops software solutions for electronic design automation (EDA), specializing in automated PCB filter design and electromagnetic simulation. The company focuses on reducing the time and engineering effort required to design and validate increasingly complex electronic components for automotive, wireless communication, and robotics applications.
Technology & Product # Its core solution, ZEPHYROS EDA, is a Python-based parametric optimization engine that automates PCB filter design by integrating with Ansys simulation tools through the PyAEDT API, including HFSS, Maxwell, and SIwave.
The platform automates key engineering tasks such as PCB geometry generation, meshing, excitation setup, three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation, design optimization, and report generation. It supports the development of low-pass filters (LPF) and band-pass filters (BPF), with simulation results stored in a proprietary component and material library for reuse in subsequent designs.
By automating repetitive design and simulation workflows, ZEPHYROS EDA aims to shorten development cycles and identify electromagnetic interference (EMI), coupling, and resonance issues before physical prototypes are manufactured.
Market & Use Cases # The technology can support automotive electronics design, PCB filter optimization, EMI/EMC engineering, RF circuit development, and electronic component validation. Potential applications include optimizing filters and electronic components for vehicle electrical and electronic (E/E) architectures, wireless connectivity, and other systems requiring reliable electromagnetic performance.
The proposed automotive application is an inferred potential use case rather than an established Mercedes-Benz collaboration. The company’s current development plan is associated with the Ansys global-collaboration track.
Traction & References # Zephyros Electronic’s founder brings more than 15 years of hands-on experience with Ansys HFSS, Maxwell, and SIwave at LG Innotek, alongside a PhD in electronics and two Jang Yeong-sil Awards. The team has developed an LPF optimization engine in Python and is advancing BPF automation and full Ansys API integration.
The company’s previous engineering work includes a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth coexistence solution combining a phase shifter and BPF-embedded PCB, reportedly reducing antenna spacing from 24 mm to 2 mm and component volume by 47%, with subsequent mass production. Commercial customers and partners include LG Innotek, SoluM, U-Tel, Vistacom, and Incheon National University. The company also reports ongoing paid engineering and software engagements.
The LPF module has been implemented and theoretically validated, while the BPF module and broader API integration remain under development. Software Version 1.0 is targeted within the relevant development agreement period; no overall TRL has been specified.
Collaboration Relevance # For Mercedes-Benz, Zephyros Electronic’s technology could potentially support faster PCB filter development and electromagnetic validation for automotive E/E hardware. By automating simulation-driven design and optimization, the platform could help engineers identify EMI and RF performance issues earlier, reduce manual engineering workload, and minimize costly PCB redesign cycles. A potential evaluation would focus on selected filter-design workflows and compatibility with existing Ansys-based engineering processes.
